# Jonathan Piper

> Jonathan Piper is a San Diego-based experimental tuba player and tubist specializing in experimental and improvisational music. He is also a creative technologist and former museum curator.

## Identity

Jonathan Piper (he/him) is an experimental tubist based in San Diego, California. His work as a performer centers on exploring sonic and gestural possibilities at the limits of the tuba and the performing body. He combines extended techniques (circular breathing, multiphonics, non-traditional mouthpieces, instrument modifications) with live electronic processing, drawing from drone, doom metal, noise, free jazz, and contemporary classical idioms.

## Active Projects

- **1515** — duo with Ryan Ebaugh (saxophone). Improvised music released on Matraca Tapes. Active in Southern California.
- **Codex Confiteor** — duo with Meghann Welsh (voice, accordion, oboe, electronics). Debut album *Syncope* on Stay Strange Records. Draws from pre-tonal Western music and contemporary improvisation.
- **go by land** — duo with Michelle Lou (bass, electronics). Large-scale, slowly evolving improvisatory music combining drone, noise, and jazz.
- **Sound Praxis** — concert series presenting experimental and improvised music at Best Practice gallery in Barrio Logan, San Diego.

## Selected Performances and Venues

High Desert Soundings, Project [BLANK] Working Title, Drone Not Drones, Some Kind of Tube, Space 4 Art, UC San Diego Music Department.

## Academic Work

- PhD in Critical Studies/Experimental Practices, University of California San Diego, 2013
- MA, University of California San Diego, 2007
- BA in Musical Performance, UCLA, 2005
- Dissertation: *Locating Experiential Richness in Doom Metal* (https://escholarship.org/uc/item/7bq7387s) — one of the first scholarly treatments of doom metal; widely cited for its analysis of groove as central to the genre

## Museum Work

From 2017 to 2023, served as curator at the NAMM Museum of Making Music (MoMM) in Carlsbad, California. Responsible for permanent and temporary exhibitions including conception, design, installation, and custom software development.
